findings.title: Rule exit behavior interpretation
findings.statement: The business rule at rule.ts:2 implements a guarded exit where the condition 'ok === false' is evaluated before returning false. This indicates that the rule only exits when the 'ok' variable is explicitly false, suggesting a design where the rule is intended to be conditionally disabled based on the 'ok' state. The implementation shows a dependency on the 'ok' variable without any explicit initialization or context, which may indicate a design assumption that 'ok' is always defined in this context.
limitations: The evidence only covers the specific line of code and does not provide broader context about the 'ok' variable's initialization or usage elsewhere in the system.
The interpretation assumes the 'ok' variable is always defined, but this is not verified by the available evidence.
The behavior described is specific to this rule and may not represent the overall business behavior pattern.
